cases.obligation: Windows distribution selects one current-user NSIS target with downgrade refusal and the owned uninstall hook.
Installer product identity and version remain exact and synchronized across Tauri, npm, and Cargo manifests.
The NSIS pre-uninstall hook can cancel without deleting autostart, while owned registry deletion is ordered only in the post-uninstall hook.
The installed production executable exposes a typed status command with an explicit artifact path and a distinct quit command.
Installed acceptance quit rejects trailing arguments rather than broadening the process-mode interface.
Installed acceptance control is unavailable unless the disposable-runner token is exact.
Installed release status and quit modes reject unset and wrong tokens without artifacts, Engine termination, or autostart mutation.
A disposable runner validates self-signed Authenticode, silent current-user installation to a spaced path, exact Run quoting, StartupApproved, and uninstall registration cleanup.
Installed release Engine and Settings coexist, Settings is single-instance, real close removes its WebView tree while Engine survives, and authenticated Quit stops Engine without changing autostart.
A running installed Engine survives a deliberately cancelled production uninstall with its executable and both autostart values intact.

Stopped-Engine log snapshots retain every relative path and exact byte hash across reinstall and uninstall, clean shutdown removes its live secret, and an installer-unowned config sentinel remains byte-exact.
Installed release Engine resources and actual process descendants, Settings footprint, startup, close, and quit remain within recorded Windows KPI gates with no Engine WebView2 descendant.
The production Windows callback core composes capture, native owner, and wakeup disposition with zero allocation, fixed lane bounds, and fail-open behavior under saturation.
